title: NBA releases ₹2.82 crore of ABS funds to 27 State Biodiversity Boards, 3 UT Biodiversity Councils and ICAR-Indian Institute of Horticultural Research, Karnataka
body_text:
The National Biodiversity Authority (NBA) has disbursed ₹2.82 crores under the Access and Benefit-Sharing (ABS) mechanism arising from the utilisation of India’s biological resources. Of this, ₹2.80 crores has been released to 27 State Biodiversity Boards (SBBs) and 3 Union Territory Biodiversity Councils (UTBCs), while ₹2.01 lakh is being released to the ICAR-Indian Institute of Horticultural Research (ICAR-IIHR), Karnataka.
The NBA received ₹2.94 crores from M/s Advanta Enterprises Ltd. (formerly M/s UPL Limited) towards ABS for the utilisation of genetic resources associated with eight hybrids of cauliflower ( Brassica oleracea var. botrytis ), five hybrids of hot pepper ( Capsicum annuum ), five hybrids of okra ( Abelmoschus esculentus ) and six hybrids of tomato ( Solanum lycopersicum ).
In this case, the biological resources were accessed through an acquisition of another company and could not be traced to benefit claimers like specific individual farmers, communities or a single identifiable geographic source. Earlier, NBA constituted an Expert Committee (EC) to recommend an appropriate modality for sharing / utilizing the benefit sharing component in such cases and the recommendation of the EC was subsequently approved by the Authority. In accordance with the approved modality, ₹2.80 crores were disbursed by the NBA. The allocation has been made taking into account the cultivation of the concerned horticultural crops across different States and Union Territories. Gujarat, West Bengal and Madhya Pradesh are among the major recipient States, with the ten States receiving the largest shares being as follows:
S.No. State Amount Released ( ₹ in lakh) 1 Gujarat 44.59 2 West Bengal 41.24 3 Madhya Pradesh 32.73 4 Odisha 32.57 5 Bihar 30.86 6 Chhattisgarh 16.54 7 Uttar Pradesh 12.66 8 Andhra Pradesh 10.51 9 Tamil Nadu 10.49 10 Maharashtra 07.07 11 Others (20 SBBs/UTBCs) 40.55
The funds released to the SBBs and UTBCs are to be utilised for activities, including documentation and updation of People's Biodiversity Registers, in-situ and ex-situ conservation, restoration of degraded ecosystems, strengthening of Biodiversity Heritage Sites, capacity building of Biodiversity Management Committees, and community livelihood enhancement, and must submit a utilisation certificate and expenditure statement within one year of receipt.
Separately, the NBA received ₹7.15 lakh from M/s Sumitomo Chemical India Ltd., Mumbai (formerly M/s Excel Crop Care) as an ABS amount towards access to two microbial strains, namely Pseudomonas fluorescens 1% WP (strain IIHR-Pf-2) and Trichoderma harzianum 1% WP (strain IIHR-Th-2), sourced from the ICAR-Indian Institute of Horticultural Research (ICAR-IIHR), Karnataka, for research and commercial utilisation. As the biological resources in this case were accessed from public research institution, 30% of the ABS amount ie., ₹2.01 lakh is being disbursed to the concerned institution ICAR-IIHR in accordance with the modalities and the rest of the fund to be utilised as per the Section 27 of the Biological Diversity Act by the NBA.
The institution is required to utilise the funds within one year for activities including maintenance of repositories, research and biodiversity survey work, capacity building in taxonomy and conservation, and in-situ and ex-situ conservation of the biological resources and their wild relatives. The disbursement is part of the NBA’s continuing efforts to strengthen the implementation of the Biological Diversity Act, 2002, and its associated regulatory framework, while ensuring that benefits arising from the commercial utilisation of India’s biological resources are channelled towards biodiversity conservation, sustainable use and the socio economic development of the farmers, local communities and others associated with the conservation and sustainable use of biological diversity.
The total ABS amount released so far by NBA is ₹ 185 crores (USD 19.34 m n). The initiative also contributes to India’s commitments under the Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD) and the Nagoya Protocol on Access and Benefit-sharing, as well as the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (KMGBF), particularly Target 13, which calls for effective measures to ensure fair and equitable sharing of benefits arising from the utilisation of genetic resources and digital sequence information on genetic resources, as applicable.
***
VM/SK

ministry.name: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change

enrichment.summary: The National Biodiversity Authority (NBA) has disbursed ₹2.82 crore under India's Access and Benefit-Sharing (ABS) mechanism, with ₹2.80 crore going to 27 State Biodiversity Boards and 3 UT Biodiversity Councils, and ₹2.01 lakh to ICAR-Indian Institute of Horticultural Research (IIHR), Karnataka. The funds originated from ABS payments by Advanta Enterprises (for hybrid seed genetic resources) and Sumitomo Chemical India (for two microbial strains sourced from ICAR-IIHR). Gujarat, West Bengal and Madhya Pradesh received the largest shares among states, and the total ABS amount disbursed by NBA to date now stands at ₹185 crore.
enrichment.context:
The Access and Benefit-Sharing (ABS) mechanism is a core pillar of India's Biological Diversity Act, 2002, which implements the country's obligations under the Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD) and its Nagoya Protocol. Under this framework, any entity commercially utilising India's biological resources or associated traditional knowledge must obtain approval from the NBA and share a percentage of resulting benefits, which are then routed to State Biodiversity Boards, Biodiversity Management Committees and, where traceable, local communities or research institutions for conservation and livelihood activities. This case is notable because the biological resources (used in vegetable hybrids) could not be traced to specific farmers or a single geographic source, having been acquired through a corporate merger/acquisition — prompting NBA to constitute an Expert Committee to devise a proportional, crop-cultivation-based allocation formula across states, a governance innovation for handling such ambiguous provenance cases.

The release also cites alignment with Target 13 of the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (KMGBF), adopted in 2022, which calls for fair and equitable sharing of benefits from genetic resources, including digital sequence information. This links India's domestic biodiversity law to its international commitments and illustrates the operationalisation of benefit-sharing principles nearly two decades after the Biological Diversity Act was enacted, with cumulative disbursements reaching ₹185 crore.

prelims_questions.question: The 'Access and Benefit-Sharing' (ABS) mechanism mentioned in news is associated with the implementation of which of the following?
options: The Biological Diversity Act, 2002 and the Nagoya Protocol
prelims_questions.explanation: The ABS mechanism operationalises India's obligations under the Nagoya Protocol to the Convention on Biological Diversity through the domestic Biological Diversity Act, 2002, implemented by the National Biodiversity Authority.

prelims_questions.question: Which of the following is a function of the National Biodiversity Authority (NBA) as per the release?
options: Granting patents for genetically modified crops
Regulating access to biological resources and disbursing benefit-sharing funds to State Biodiversity Boards
Issuing environmental clearances for industrial projects
Notifying protected areas under the Wildlife Protection Act
prelims_questions.explanation: The release describes NBA regulating access to India's biological resources for commercial use and disbursing the resulting ABS funds to State Biodiversity Boards, UT Biodiversity Councils and research institutions.

mains_questions.question: Discuss the significance of the Access and Benefit-Sharing (ABS) mechanism under the Biological Diversity Act, 2002 in ensuring equitable sharing of benefits from India's genetic resources. What challenges arise when the source of biological resources cannot be traced to specific communities?
Examine the role of the National Biodiversity Authority in implementing India's commitments under the Nagoya Protocol and the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework.

study_notes.reason: The release carries a testable factual core (NBA, Biological Diversity Act 2002, ABS mechanism, Nagoya Protocol, KMGBF Target 13) while also offering a genuine governance puzzle — how to share benefits when biological resources cannot be traced to a specific source — which is rich analytical material for GS2/GS3.

prelims.point: National Biodiversity Authority (NBA) is a statutory body under the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change, established under the Biological Diversity Act, 2002
prelims.syllabus: GS Paper 2 - Statutory and Regulatory Bodies
prelims.why_important: NBA's parent Act and ministry are classic objective-question material, especially distinguishing it from State Biodiversity Boards and Biodiversity Management Committees.

prelims.point: Access and Benefit-Sharing (ABS) mechanism under the Biological Diversity Act, 2002 requires entities commercially utilising Indian biological resources or traditional knowledge to share benefits, routed via NBA to State Biodiversity Boards/UT Biodiversity Councils/institutions
prelims.why_important: Tests understanding of the three-tier institutional structure (NBA-SBB-BMC) and the flow of ABS funds, a recurring conceptual area.

prelims.point: India's ABS framework implements obligations under the Nagoya Protocol to the Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD)
prelims.why_important: Links a domestic law to a specific international protocol, a favourite UPSC pairing question (which protocol relates to which convention).

prelims.point: Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (KMGBF), adopted 2022, Target 13 deals with fair and equitable sharing of benefits from genetic resources including digital sequence information
prelims.why_important: KMGBF targets are increasingly tested; knowing Target 13's specific subject (benefit-sharing) helps distinguish it from other numbered targets like 30x30 (Target 3).

prelims.point: Under Section 27 of the Biological Diversity Act, when biological resources are accessed from a public research institution, 30% of the ABS amount is disbursed to that institution
prelims.why_important: A specific statutory percentage figure that could be tested as a factual detail distinguishing institution-linked versus untraceable-resource cases.

prelims.point: Cumulative ABS disbursement by NBA to date stands at ₹185 crore
prelims.why_important: A benchmark figure that could appear in a 'which of the following is correct about NBA's ABS disbursement' type question.

mains.point: NBA had to constitute an Expert Committee to devise a proportional, crop-cultivation-based allocation formula when biological resources acquired via corporate merger/acquisition could not be traced to specific farmers or a geographic source
mains.analytical_use: Useful for a question on challenges in implementing access and benefit-sharing frameworks, or on adapting regulatory mechanisms to ambiguous provenance in a globalised seed/biotech market.

mains.point: ABS funds are earmarked for concrete conservation and livelihood activities — People's Biodiversity Registers, in-situ/ex-situ conservation, restoration of degraded ecosystems, Biodiversity Heritage Sites, and community livelihood enhancement — with mandatory utilisation certificates
mains.analytical_use: Supports answers on how legal/financial mechanisms translate into decentralised biodiversity conservation and community welfare, and on accountability safeguards (utilisation certificates).

mains.point: The case illustrates tension between corporate consolidation of genetic resource rights (via mergers/acquisitions) and India's sovereign benefit-sharing claims over biological resources
mains.analytical_use: Relevant for questions on protecting national biodiversity interests against corporate exploitation and the adequacy of the Biological Diversity Act in a globalised agribusiness context.

mains.point: India's ABS operationalisation nearly two decades after the 2002 Act, now aligned with KMGBF Target 13, demonstrates slow but incremental institutionalisation of benefit-sharing commitments
mains.theme: International commitments and domestic implementation gap
mains.analytical_use: Useful for evaluating the pace and effectiveness of translating international biodiversity commitments (CBD, Nagoya Protocol, KMGBF) into functioning domestic mechanisms.

low_priority.reason: Granular disbursement figures for individual states carry no conceptual or testable value beyond noting top recipients.

low_priority.point: Names of specific hybrid crop varieties (eight cauliflower hybrids, five hot pepper hybrids, etc.) and company name changes (UPL to Advanta, Excel Crop Care to Sumitomo)
low_priority.reason: Corporate and varietal specifics are administrative detail with no exam relevance.
